name: Cable Rope Pushdown
description: The cable rope pushdown is a cable isolation exercise for the triceps using a rope attachment on a high pulley. At the bottom of the movement, the rope ends are spread apart, which supinates the wrists slightly and creates a wider range of motion compared to a bar attachment. This spreading action produces a more complete contraction of all three triceps heads, particularly the lateral head, making it a popular finisher exercise.

execution.starting_position: Attach a rope to the high pulley. Grip one end in each hand with a neutral grip, thumbs up. Stand facing the cable stack with the elbows bent at 90 degrees and tucked to the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the cable to the highest position. Attach a rope handle. Grip the knots at each end of the rope. Stand close enough that the cable is taut at the starting position.
steps: Step 1: Grip the rope ends, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees and pinned at the sides.
Step 2: Keep the upper arms stationary throughout — only the forearms move.
Step 3: Exhale and press the rope downward by extending the elbows. As the arms approach full extension, spread the rope ends outward and slightly apart.
Step 4: Hold the peak contraction with the arms fully extended and the rope spread, then inhale and return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pushdown; inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Not spreading the rope at the bottom, which reduces the range of contraction
Letting the elbows drift forward away from the sides during the movement
safety_considerations: Keep wrists neutral throughout — do not flex or hyperextend them under load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension with rope spread at the bottom; elbows at 90 degrees at the top.
coaching_cues: Spread the rope ends at the bottom like you are trying to touch each hip
Elbows stay pinned to your sides — they are the fulcrum, not the driver
